title: Autofocus row shows an editable 'method' chip that the executor ignores, next to a panel saying the real method is something else
what_happened: An Autofocus node's tree row renders 'Autofocus | [vCurve v] | uses defaults'. The Properties panel for the same node, visible at the same time, shows 'Use Settings Defaults [ON] - Using global AF settings' and then 'Global settings: Method = Star HFR, Curve Fitting = Hyperbolic'. I opened the row chip and changed it to 'quadratic'; the row became 'quadratic | uses defaults' and the panel still said Star HFR / Hyperbolic. The chosen value was persisted to the DB (properties {"method":"quadratic",...,"useSettingsDefaults":true}) but per capture_and_guiding.dart:371-374 and autofocus_controls.dart:87-96 it is discarded at run time whenever useSettingsDefaults is true, which is the default.
expected: When 'Use Settings Defaults' is on, the row should show the method that will actually run (Star HFR) or show nothing, and the chip should be disabled. An editable control that has no effect and displays a value contradicted by the panel beside it is a false statement about what the run will do.
repro: Sequencer > Builder > palette search 'autofocus' > click + . Select the node. Read the tree row chip vs the Properties panel 'Global settings' block. Click the row chip and pick 'quadratic'; re-read both.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-16c-afrow.png (row: 'quadratic  uses defaults'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-16b-afpanel.png (panel: Method Star HFR, Curve Fitting Hyperbolic), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-15-afmethod.png (dropdown open, options vCurve/hyperbolic/quadratic)
proposed_fix: In node_summary.dart, when useSettingsDefaults is true emit a StaticFragment showing the effective global method rather than an EditableFragment bound to node.method; only render the editable chip when the node is in 'custom' mode. Also relabel: the node's enum values (vCurve/hyperbolic/quadratic) are curve-fit choices, while the global setting distinguishes Method (Star HFR) from Curve Fitting (Hyperbolic) - the node model conflates two different settings under one name.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on display :84, profile sequencer-build-verify. Added an Autofocus node: the tree row renders 'Autofocus | [vCurve v] uses defaults' while the Properties panel on the same screen shows 'Use Settings Defaults [ON] - Using global AF settings' and 'Global settings (edit in Settings > Autofocus): Method = Star HFR, Curve Fitting = Hyperbolic' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/sbv-07-afadded.png). The chip is a live dropdown offering vCurve/hyperbolic/quadratic (sbv-08-afdrop.png); selecting 'quadratic' changed the row to 'quadratic uses defaults' while the panel still read Star HFR / Hyperbolic (sbv-09-afquad.png). Code confirms the consequence: node_summary.dart:290-297 emits EditableFragment(InlineEditKind.autofocusMethod, method.name) unconditionally, and the executor discards it - serialization_operations.dart:405-417 passes nodeOverrides: n.useSettingsDefaults ? null : n, with useSettingsDefaults defaulting to true (capture_and_guiding.dart:402); device_service/autofocus_controls.dart:96-107 then overwrites effectiveMethod from appSettings.afMethod. Severity corrected P1->P2: the statement is false and the control is dead, but the truthful value is displayed inches away in the same view and an AF-method mismatch does not lose a run's data.

title: Target header card under-reports planned exposures and integration time by the loop multiplier - including for every sequence the app's own Quick-Start Wizard builds
what_happened: I ran the Quick-Start Wizard end to end (M31, 120s, count 10). It produced a Capture Loop with repeatCount 10 containing a single 'Light 1 x 120s' exposure node, all under the M31 TargetHeader. The toolbar reported '10 frames' and the DB stored estimated_duration_mins = 20 (correct). The M31 target header card on the same screen reported 'Ready / 1 planned exposures - 2m'. Ten-fold understatement of both the frame count and the integration time, on the card the user reads to decide whether the night's plan is right.
expected: '10 planned exposures - 20m', matching the toolbar frame count and the stored estimate.
repro: Sequencer > Templates > Quick-Start Wizard. Step 1: RA 0.712, Dec 41.27, name M31. Next through steps 2-5 with defaults. Create Sequence. Read the M31 target card status line, then scroll down to see 'Capture Loop x10 > Light 1 x 120s', then read the toolbar frame counter.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-52-qsbuilt.png ('1 planned exposures - 2m' + toolbar '10 frames'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-54-qstree2.png (Capture Loop x10 containing Light 1x120s), sqlite dump of sequence_nodes for sequence_id=3 showing Loop {"conditionType":"count","repeatCount":10} as the parent of the TakeExposure {"count":1}
proposed_fix: Give visit() a multiplier argument and multiply by LoopNode.repeatCount for count-type loops, exactly as Sequence._countExposures does at sequence_state.dart:168-188. Better: delete _calculateTargetPlan and reuse the model's counting so the two can never diverge again.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end. Ran the Quick-Start Wizard (RA 0.712, Dec 41.27, name M31, 120s, defaults through steps 2-5) and pressed Create Sequence. The built tree is 'Capture Loop x10' containing 'Light 1 x 120s' (sbv-52-tree2.png); the toolbar frame counter reads '10 frames' and the M31 target header card on the same screen reads 'Ready / 1 planned exposures - 2m' (sbv-50-m31seq.png). Saving it stored estimated_duration_mins = 20 for that sequence (sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-build-verify/data/skotiq.db 'select id,name,estimated_duration_mins from sequences' -> 2|M31 Sequence|20). So toolbar and DB agree at 10 frames / 20m and only the target card is 10x low. Code matches the named location: target_header_card.dart _calculateTargetPlan's visit() (~lines 675-706) recurses into childIds with no loop multiplier, unlike Sequence._countExposures (sequence_state.dart:168-188) which multiplies by LoopNode.repeatCount for count-type loops. Severity corrected P1->P2: it is a false plan summary but display-only, and the correct figure is shown in the toolbar beside it.

title: Sequence Library card reports 10m for a 20-frame sequence - Smart Exposure integration is dropped from the stored duration
what_happened: Built a sequence containing one Take Exposures (10 x 60s) and one Smart Exposure (L, 10 x 60s). The Builder header estimated '~39m 45s' and the toolbar counted '20 frames'. Saving it to the library produced a card reading '2 exposures - 10m', and sequences.estimated_duration_mins in the DB is 10. Bare integration alone is 20 x 60s = 20 minutes. The stored figure equals exactly the ExposureNode contribution (600s); the SmartExposureNode contributes nothing.
expected: The card duration should reflect all imaging nodes. 20 min integration (or the ~40 min run estimate the Builder shows) - anything but half.
repro: Sequencer > Builder > add 'Take Exposures' and 'Smart Exposure' from the palette. Note the Builder header estimate and the toolbar frame count. Sequences tab > Save Current > name it > Save. Read the new card's duration chip, then: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/<profile>/data/skotiq.db 'select name,estimated_duration_mins from sequences;'
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-33-saved.png (card 'M31 | 12 nodes | 1 targets | 2 exposures | 10m'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-07-search-dither.png (Builder header '~39m 30s', toolbar '20 frames'), DB: sequences row 1 estimated_duration_mins=10
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/sequence/sequence_models/sequence_state.dart:315-322 (_estimateNodeIntegration handles ExposureNode only); persisted via packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_repository.dart:208 and :239
proposed_fix: Add a SmartExposureNode branch to _estimateNodeIntegration using node.totalIntegrationSecs (already defined at smart_exposure_node.dart:84), mirroring what Sequence.totalExposures already does for the frame count. Note the same stored value feeds LongEstimatedDurationRule (settings_rules.dart:158) and the disk-space rule, so both are currently under-estimating.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with the exact stated setup. Built a sequence containing Take Exposures (10 x 60s) and Smart Exposure (L, 10 x 60s); the toolbar read '20 frames' (sbv-13-built.png). Saved via Sequences > Save Current; the card reads '5 nodes | 0 targets | 2 exposures | 10m' (sbv-16-saved.png) and the DB row is 1|New Sequence|10. Bare integration is 20 x 60s = 20 min, so the stored value is exactly the ExposureNode contribution (600s) and SmartExposureNode contributes nothing. Code confirms: sequence_state.dart _estimateNodeIntegration (starting line 302) has an ExposureNode branch only and no SmartExposureNode branch, while SmartExposureNode (advanced_nodes/smart_exposure_node.dart:84) does expose totalIntegrationSecs; sequence_repository.dart:208/:239 persist (sequence.totalIntegrationSecs / 60).ceil(). One sub-claim is wrong: the finding says the same stored value also feeds the disk-space rule - disk_space_rules.dart contains no reference to estimatedDurationMins/totalIntegrationSecs. LongEstimatedDurationRule (settings_rules.dart:157) does read sequence.estimatedDurationMins, as claimed. Severity corrected P1->P2 (display/estimate only, no run impact). Note the file path in 'where' is right but the exact line range 315-322 is approximate.

title: Every keyboard shortcut the sequencer advertises is dead in the ordinary state - including the Ctrl+Z that two delete dialogs say is the only recovery
what_happened: The sequencer's own Keyboard Shortcuts sheet (5th tab) lists Alt+1..4, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Delete, Esc. With an Autofocus node selected (Properties panel showing it) I pressed Delete: nothing. Ctrl+D: nothing. Ctrl+Z after a confirmed node deletion: nothing (the deleted node stayed gone; the toolbar Undo button restored it immediately after). Alt+2, Alt+3 and Ctrl+T never switched tab, even after clicking directly on the tree canvas. The bindings only fired after I clicked a tab-bar button, which happens to move focus into the subtree - Ctrl+D then duplicated correctly (10 -> 11 steps). The delete confirmation dialog states 'This cannot be undone except via Undo (Ctrl+Z)', which is false in exactly the state a user reaches it from (they just typed in the palette search to find the node they are now deleting - that TextField keeps focus and swallows the keys).
expected: Shortcuts listed in the help sheet work whenever the Sequencer screen is showing, regardless of which widget last received a click; and the delete dialog's recovery instruction must be accurate.
repro: Sequencer > Builder > palette search 'delay' > add > click any node row to select it (Properties panel updates) > press Delete, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Z: nothing happens. Now click 'Sequences' then 'Builder' in the tab bar, click a node, press Ctrl+D: it duplicates. Then press Alt+3 at any time: the tab does not change.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-13-selstate.png (Autofocus selected, Delete/Ctrl+D/Ctrl+Z all no-op), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-94-tab5.png (the shortcuts sheet), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-95-alt3.png (still on Builder after Alt+3 with a node selected), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-10-delete.png (the 'cannot be undone except via Undo (Ctrl+Z)' claim)
proposed_fix: Wrap the CallbackShortcuts subtree in a FocusScope with autofocus, or move the bindings to a Shortcuts/Actions pair registered on the route so they do not depend on a descendant holding primary focus. Make the tree rows themselves focusable so clicking one moves focus into the scope. Until Ctrl+Z is reliable, change the delete-dialog copy to point at the toolbar Undo button, which does work.
verdict_reasoning: The mechanism reproduces, but the title overstates the scope. Confirmed: after clicking the palette 'Search nodes...' TextField and then clicking a node row to select it (Properties panel updates), Ctrl+D and Delete are both no-ops (node count stayed 2 nodes / 1 step), and Alt+3 does not switch tab. Clicking the empty tree canvas afterwards does NOT restore them - Alt+3 still dead (tree still shows 'Tab 1 of 3' toolbox, no Sequence Library). Confirmed the recovery path: after clicking a tab-bar button (Sequences then Builder), Alt+3 did switch to Sequence Library. Confirmed the sheet contents: the 5th tab renders 'Keyboard Shortcuts' listing Alt+1..4, Ctrl+T/Z/Y/D/C/V, Delete, Esc (sbv-56-shortcuts.png). Confirmed the false copy: 'This cannot be undone except via Undo (Ctrl+Z).' appears at delete_node_confirmation.dart:70-75 and batch_operations_toolbar.dart:221-223. REFUTED sub-claim: the shortcuts are not dead 'in the ordinary state' generally - they work whenever focus is inside the CallbackShortcuts subtree (fresh entry / after any tab-bar click); they die specifically once the palette search TextField (or another out-of-scope focusable) takes primary focus. Severity corrected P1->P2: keyboard-only regression with a working toolbar Undo, plus one inaccurate dialog sentence.

title: Exposure Triggers dialog lets you add and Save a trigger, then silently discards it when the selected node cannot hold triggers
what_happened: With the root 'Sequence' InstructionSet selected I clicked the toolbar bell (Exposure Triggers). The dialog opened, 'Add Trigger' created 'Guiding RMS > 2.0" -> Pause & Recalibrate', and Save closed the dialog with no error. Reopening the dialog showed 'No triggers configured'. Repeating the identical steps with a Take Exposures node selected persisted the trigger correctly. The button is enabled regardless of selection and the dialog gives no indication which node it is editing.
expected: Either disable the toolbar button (with a tooltip: 'select an exposure node') when the selection cannot hold triggers, or tell the user on Save that nothing was stored. Silently accepting and dropping a safety trigger is the worst of the three options - a user who set 'abort if guiding RMS > 2"' would believe they are protected.
repro: Sequencer > Builder > click the root 'Sequence' row > toolbar bell icon > Add Trigger > Save > click the bell again: 'No triggers configured'. Now add a Take Exposures node, select it, and repeat: the trigger is there on reopen.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-74-addtrigger.png (trigger created), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-76-trigreopen.png ('No triggers configured' after Save+reopen, root selected), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-78-trig2.png (same steps with an exposure node selected: trigger persists)
proposed_fix: Resolve the target exposure node up front; if none, disable the toolbar action and put the reason in the tooltip. Show the owning node's name in the dialog subtitle so the user knows what they are editing.
verdict_reasoning: The user-visible defect is real but the stated cause is wrong. REFUTED as written: with the root 'Sequence' InstructionSet selected in a sequence that contained a Take Exposures node, I added 'Guiding RMS > 2.0" -> Pause & Recalibrate', pressed Save, and on reopening the dialog the trigger was still there (sbv-27-trigreopen.png). Selection is irrelevant. CONFIRMED under the real condition: on a sequence with NO ExposureNode (fresh New Sequence, 1 node / 0 steps) the identical steps - Add Trigger (sbv-31-trigadd2.png), Save, reopen - show 'No triggers configured' (sbv-33-trigreopen2.png) with no error. Code explains both: sequence_toolbar.dart:166-195 openExposureTriggers writes the result into every ExposureNode in the sequence via `for (final node in current.nodes.values.whereType<ExposureNode>())`, and currentExposureTriggers() (:156-164) reads from the first ExposureNode; with zero exposure nodes both are no-ops while the success snackbar still fires. The proposed fix (resolve the target exposure node up front, disable with a reason when none) is still the right fix. Severity corrected P1->P2: it only drops the trigger on a sequence that has no exposure node at all, i.e. one that cannot image anything yet.

title: 'Collapse all' paints a solid grey block over the rest of the sequence tree
what_happened: Clicking the header's 'Collapse' toggle on a 28-node sequence collapses the first two rows correctly and then replaces everything below with one opaque light-grey rectangle filling the remaining tree viewport. The header still reports '28 nodes' and the root still reports '5 steps', so only rendering is broken. It persists across re-screenshots 5s and 20s later. Clicking 'Expand' restores normal rendering; collapsing again reproduces it.
expected: Collapse-all shows one compact row per top-level node.
repro: Sequencer > Builder with a sequence containing at least one nested container (e.g. a Photometry Run template) > click 'Collapse' in the tree header. Wait 5s and look.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/sequence_tree/support_widgets.dart (_CollapseAllToggle) and the tree's collapsed-row rendering path
proposed_fix: Likely a collapsed row reporting an unbounded/zero intrinsic height that the list then paints as a bare Container. Reproduce under a debug build with the layout explorer on a sequence containing a nested container plus a LiveStacking node.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently. Built a 9-node sequence containing a nested container (Photometry Run template, 3 steps) and clicked the tree header's 'Collapse' toggle: the rows above the container render normally and everything from the collapsed container row down is replaced by one opaque light-grey rectangle filling the remaining tree viewport (sbv-23-collapse.png). Header still reports '9 nodes' and root '5 steps', so state is intact and only painting is wrong; still present 12s later (sbv-24-collapse2.png). Toggle label flips to 'Expand'. Location claim checks out: _CollapseAllToggle exists at sequence_tree/support_widgets.dart:887, wired from sequence_header.dart:232. CAVEAT worth recording: both observations (the original sweep's and mine) are on the same softpipe/Xvfb rasterizer, so a Mesa softpipe artifact has not been ruled out - this needs one look on a real GPU before a fix is designed. Severity P2 upheld.

title: Multi-select highlights three rows but the batch bar and the delete confirmation both say two
what_happened: Clicked 'Change Filter' (becomes the primary selection, shown in Properties), then Ctrl+clicked 'Live Stacking' and 'Center Target'. All three rows render with an identical cyan selection border at full zoom, but the batch toolbar reads '2 selected' and pressing its Delete opens 'Delete 2 node(s)?'. The primary selection is drawn as selected while being excluded from every batch operation, and there is no visual difference between the two states.
expected: Either the primary selection joins the multi-select set (count 3), or it is drawn differently (e.g. outline vs fill) so the count and the highlight agree.
repro: Sequencer > Builder > click a node row > Ctrl+click two more rows > compare the highlighted row count with the '<n> selected' chip, then click Delete and read the dialog title.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-62-multisel3.png ('2 selected', three rows outlined), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-64-rows.png (2x zoom: identical borders), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-65-batchdelconf.png ('Delete 2 node(s)?')
proposed_fix: Make the first Ctrl+click seed the multi-select set with the existing primary selection (the behaviour every file manager has), or give multiSelectedNodeIds a visually distinct row treatment.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Clicked one Autofocus row (primary selection, shown in Properties), then Ctrl+clicked two more rows. A raw 1:1 capture shows three rows drawn with an identical cyan selection border (sbv-19-multisel3.png) while the batch bar reads '2 selected' (sbv-20-batchbar.png). I also caught the intermediate state: 2 rows outlined, bar reading '1 selected'. The delete-title claim is confirmed in code: batch_operations_toolbar.dart:210 sets count = selectedIds.length (the multi-select set, excluding the primary) and :229 renders 'Delete $count node(s)?'. So the primary selection is painted identically to the multi-selected rows while being excluded from every batch operation. Severity P2 upheld.

title: Mosaic Wizard invents a camera field of view and plans the whole mosaic from it, while the framing dialog on the same screen correctly refuses to guess
what_happened: With no equipment profile configured, the Mosaic Wizard's Plan summary states 'Panel size: 1.00 deg x 0.67 deg' and derives 'Active panels 9 / Grid 3x3 / Est. time 2.3 h / Total exposures 90' from it. Those degrees are the hardcoded field defaults _panelWidthArcmin = 60.0 / _panelHeightArcmin = 40.0, not anything measured from the user's rig. The 'Frame target' dialog, reachable from the same Builder screen, handles the identical missing data honestly: 'No equipment profile with a focal length - set one in Settings to size the framing box.'
expected: Say the FOV is unknown and require a focal length / sensor size (or an explicit override) before quoting a panel size, panel count and total time as facts.
repro: Sequencer > Builder (no equipment profile) > toolbar grid icon (Plan Mosaic). Read 'Panel size' in the Plan summary. Then select a Target node and click 'Frame target' and read its warning.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-79-mosaic.png ('Panel size: 1.00 deg x 0.67 deg'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-22-frame.png (framing dialog admits it cannot size the box)
proposed_fix: Initialise the panel size from the active equipment profile's focal length + sensor dimensions. When that is unavailable, show 'unknown' with the same wording the framing dialog uses and disable 'Load into Sequencer' / 'Create mosaic project' until it is supplied.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with no equipment profile configured. The Mosaic Wizard's Plan summary states 'Active panels 9 / Grid 3x3 / Panel size: 1.00 deg x 0.67 deg / Overlap 10% / Est. time (14m/panel x 10 subs): 2.3 h / Total exposures: 90' (sbv-43-mosaic.png). Those degrees are exactly the hardcoded field initialisers _panelWidthArcmin = 60.0 and _panelHeightArcmin = 40.0 at mosaic_wizard_dialog.dart:64-65; initState (:105-129) sets only _centerRa/_centerDec and never reads an equipment profile, focal length or sensor size. The contrast claim also holds: the Frame-target dialog on the same Builder screen says 'Field of view unknown - No equipment profile with a focal length - set one in Settings to size the framing box.' (sbv-44-frame.png). One mitigating fact the finding omits: the panel size IS user-editable in the wizard's Advanced section (callback at :891-898), so this is an invented default presented as fact rather than an unchangeable one. Severity P2 upheld.

title: Library cards count exposure NODES and call them 'exposures'; the same card's preview then says 'No exposures'
what_happened: A saved sequence containing 20 planned frames (Take Exposures 10 + Smart Exposure 10) shows the chip '2 exposures'. The wizard-built M31 Sequence, which plans 10 frames, shows '1 exposures'. The number is a count of nodes whose specificType is an exposure type, presented with a word that every astrophotographer reads as 'frames'. Expanding the same card's Preview shows 'M31 / No exposures', so one card contradicts itself. 'n targets' is also not pluralised ('1 targets').
expected: '20 frames' (matching the Builder toolbar's own frame counter), and a preview that agrees with the chip.
repro: Sequencer > Sequences tab. Compare each card's 'n exposures' chip with the Builder toolbar's 'n frames' for the same sequence, then click the chevron to expand the card preview.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-33-saved.png ('2 exposures' vs toolbar '20 frames'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-34-cardpreview.png (preview: 'No exposures'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-104-lib3.png ('1 exposures' for a 10-frame sequence, '1 targets')
proposed_fix: Persist a frame total alongside estimated_duration_mins (Sequence.totalExposures already computes it with loop multipliers) and label the chip 'frames'. Pluralise targets. Make the preview walk the same node set as the chips.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on two saved sequences. A 20-frame sequence (Take Exposures 10 + Smart Exposure 10) shows the chip '2 exposures' against the Builder toolbar's '20 frames'; the wizard-built M31 Sequence, which plans 10 frames, shows '1 exposures' and '1 targets' (sbv-53-lib2.png). Expanding the first card's preview gives 'No targets - 1 exposure node.' - the same card saying 2 in the chip and 1 in the preview (sbv-17-preview.png). Code confirms both halves: sequences_dao.dart:151-153 computes exposureCount as sequenceNodes.id.count(filter: specificType.isIn(_exposureSpecificTypes)) i.e. a node count, rendered as '${_summary.exposureCount} exposures' at sequence_card.dart:247-250 alongside an unpluralised '${_summary.targetCount} targets'; the preview body (:451-457) and _buildTargetPreviewRow's walk (:477-500) both use whereType<ExposureNode>() only, which is why a SmartExposure-only target renders 'No exposures' (:527). Severity P2 upheld.
